description: Runs an elementary cellular automaton over 16 cells and 16 generations, and reads four of those generations out as gates one cell at a time

params.text: Picks the cellular automaton rule, a whole number from 0 to 255
Picks a new rule at random and writes it into the rule knob; a further press is ignored for one second
Sets the 16 cells of the first generation as a whole number from 0 to 65535
Picks a new first generation at random and writes it into the seed knob; a further press is ignored for one second
Chooses which four consecutive generations feed the four outputs, 0 to 3
Holds the read position at the first cell for as long as the button is pressed

inputs.text: A rising edge moves the read position on by one cell, wrapping after sixteen
0 to 5V picks the rule from 0 to 255, overriding the rule knob while it is patched
A rising edge picks a new rule at random, no more than once a second
0 to 5V picks the first generation from 0 to 65535, overriding the seed knob while it is patched
A rising edge picks a new first generation at random, no more than once a second
0 to 3V picks which four generations feed the outputs, overriding the window knob while it is patched
A rising edge moves the read position back to the first cell

outputs.text: Carries 5V while the cell under the read position is on in its own generation, and 0V while that cell is off

notes: the grid is a drawing of the automaton with the read position and the chosen window marked on it; clicking it does nothing
changing the rule or the seed recomputes all sixteen generations from the first, and leaves the read position where it was
the window reaches only generations 0 to 6 of the sixteen the module computes; the rest never reach an output
the two random jacks share one edge detector in the source, so patching both makes each one steal the other's triggers
